summary: Four of the 13 misses were Bitcoin price levels called at 77% to 94% three to six days before one sharp fall; in two of them the exchange's price and volatility could not be read that day. The rest were close calls or one-off events.

misses.note: Near-even race on tied polls; the narrow Democratic win was within polling error.
A disrupted plot that included the person was read as unlikely to count, but the rule was wide enough to allow it.
Exchange price read on the forecast day; 77% matched the three-day base rate and the price then fell below the level within three days.
Needed a further 8 cents in five days; the fall was a little faster than the trend.
Modest lean to a beat on an unverified consensus; the miss was within ordinary earnings noise.
A near coin flip on an unverified consensus; the company beat.
Exchange price read on the forecast day; 94% sat above its own 89% five-day base rate during a month-long fall, and the price dropped more than 7.5% in five days.
Finalist list was never found, so the entrant's place and the final's date stayed unconfirmed.
The exchange's price and volatility could not be read on the forecast day, so 82% rested on that day's news reports, one day after a 6% drop.
Latest print sat exactly on the threshold, so a small rise decided it.
The latest price in the research was three days old on the forecast day because exchange pages would not open, and no volatility was computed.
Travel schedule was unconfirmed and the final date was close to the edge of the window.
Forecast before the first session after results; a level the stock had come within 1% of a week earlier was given 10% with no volatility computed.

Crypto: For a price-above or price-below question more than one day ahead, give the chance from the last 7 days' realised daily volatility as well as the 30-day figure, and count how often a move of the needed size happened over the same number of days in the last 90 days; if the exchange's price or daily closes cannot be opened, say so first instead of taking the level from a news report.
Economy: For an earnings-beat question, find the exact per-share threshold and the consensus it is based on from a page you opened, with its date and the release time, and count the last 8 results against that same measure; if the threshold cannot be confirmed, say so and stay near the base rate.
